messages:
maria: heads-up, ap-se1 is seeing a weird small-pod carousel — lots of 0.5 GPU pods Pending for >10m even when capacity looks free on some nodes
kevin: any taint changes or label rollouts recently?
maria: we rolled label rollout cluster-wide 15m ago: node.k8s.redwood/zone-weight=low -> deprecated=false (via automation)
maria: kubectl get pods -n infra | grep Pending | wc -l -> 42
maria: sample pod: 
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: tiny-train-abc
spec:
  containers:
  - name: worker
    resources:
      limits:
        nvidia.com/gpu: "0.5"
    nodeSelector:
      runtime: gpu
  affinity:
    podAntiAffinity: {} # minimal
  tolerations:
  - key: "gpu.preempt"
    operator: "Exists"
```
kevin: hmm 0.5 GPU fractional requests + our scheduler plugin recently had a change to prefer full-slot packing. could be binpack heuristic now skipping nodes with small free fragments
ops-bot: @channel eviction-controller triggered: 12 graceful-preempt evictions in last 5m on ap-se1c
maria: here's `kubectl describe node ap-se1c-node-114` relevant bits: 
```
Allocated resources:  24/32 GPUs
Allocatable: 32
Free fragments:  16 slots of size 0.125-0.75 GPU
Taints: gpu.reserve=true:NoSchedule
```
jess: `gpu.reserve=true` should only be on warmpool nodes, did the reserve label accidentally propagate?
tim: ops automation set reserve taint on nodes matching /warmpool-.*/ but rollout regex might've caught a few normal nodes with similar names yesterday
kevin: also our scheduler had a preemption threshold update — it avoids preempting small fractional pods to protect latency-sensitive tiny workloads. combined with full-slot packing this can leave 0.5 requests unplaced when only fragmented free exists
maria: net result: nodes show free capacity but each fragment < requested 0.5 so scheduler reports unschedulable due to "Insufficient gpu"
jess: can we enable fractional coalescing (experimental) to allow multiple 0.125 fragments to satisfy a 0.5 request? or fallback to binpack-relaxed?
tim: fractional coalescing is currently off in ap-se1; enabling needs rollout and might risk noisy neighbor perf. Ops, what's the risk tolerance for ap-se1 today?
ops-bot: alerting: ap-se1 has 18% higher GPU wait time vs baseline. SLO impact moderate. Ops oncall @kevin ?
kevin: I'm oncall, will try a quick mitigation: 1) mark suspect nodes with taint: scheduling=drain-temp (so we'll move warmpool taint back) 2) flip scheduler to relaxed-binpack on ap-se1 for 20m 3) monitor cost impact
maria: doing kubectl taint node ap-se1-node-114 scheduling=drain-temp:NoSchedule -> applied to 6 nodes that accidentally had reserve taint
scheduler-bot: scheduler config changed: binpack_mode=relaxed on cluster ap-se1 (user=kevin, reason=evict-carousal-mitigate)
kevin: now checking pending queue, 42 -> 6 in 90s
maria: some pods started, but we see a flurry of preemptions on tiny-latency pools (5 pods)
kevin: rollback preemption threshold tweak so small pods still preemptible; patching now
tim: next step we should add an invariant check on the taint regex used by warmpool automation to prevent accidental application to normal nodes (PR incoming)
jess: also add telemetry: track fragment size distribution per AZ so we can auto-suggest warmpool size changes or enable fractional coalesce when fragmentation > X%
maria: cost note: relaxed-binpack raises immediate GPU unit cost by ~6% (more spread), but reduces waiting latency SLO breach risk
kevin: agreed acceptable for now, we'll revert in 2h unless further degradation
ops-bot: incident ticket created: INC-2026-1234, severity=sev3, owners=@kevin,@maria,@tim
maria: documenting runbook step we did:
1) identify nodes with accidental taint (label rollout misfire)
2) taint them scheduling=drain-temp to stop filling
3) flip scheduler binpack_mode to relaxed for ap-se1
4) monitor pending pods and preemption churn
5) plan long-term: enable fractional coalesce or tune warmpool sizes
kevin: postmortem action items: fix regex, add unit test on node name patterns, incremental rollout for taint changes, and small-pod packing policy per-cluster
kevin: thanks all, will follow up with PRs and a short postmortem note in incidents channel
maria: thanks — keeping watch for next 30m :heart:
